facts.text: Randwick takes its name from the English village of Randwick, the birthplace of Simeon Henry Pearce, who later founded the suburb.
Simeon Pearce built the first stone house in the area, Blenheim House, in 1848; the sandstone cottage still stands on Blenheim Street.
Randwick Racecourse began as a sandy track in 1833, later becoming the site of the Australian Jockey Club’s relocated racecourse in 1860.
Randwick was proclaimed a municipality in February 1859, a milestone that marked its transition from a rural settlement to an organized suburb.
The Randwick Line of Sydney’s light rail network ends at Randwick station, making the suburb a key terminus for commuters and tourists alike.
